I have enough verified evidence. Writing the deliverable.

# 11 — Combat/Buff Behavioral-Contract Extraction

Portable behavioral spec for RynthAi's combat + buff subsystems. Every contract is the *debugged* behavior (each traces to a specific in-game failure the reviews/comments document), stated so a reimplementation in in-page JS, C#-over-a-bridge, or Rust can be built against it. Sources: `Combat/CombatManager.cs` (3,443 L), `Combat/BuffManager.cs` (2,232 L), `Combat/CastGateWatchdog.cs`, `Combat/WeaponSwapGate.cs`, host SDK `RynthCoreHost.cs`, and the two forensic reviews.

---

## 0. The three pacing gates — the model any port must reproduce

RynthAi never uses one "busy" boolean. It composes **three orthogonal signals**, each answering a different question. Conflating them is the single most common way ports of this logic break (the review calls this out; the code documents four separate AVs caused by getting it wrong).

| Gate | Host API | Semantics | What it protects against | Fallback when absent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cast-gesture gate** (`CanCastNow`) | `GetCastBusyState()==0` — `RynthCoreHost.cs:652-663` | The **real** cast gate. Reads the client's `CMotionInterp` gesture state (`[CMI+0x80]`). `0`/true = no cast/action gesture animating → clear to issue a cast. | Issuing a 2nd cast mid-gesture → server "You're too busy!" → sustained refusals re-enter `AddTextToScroll` → **AV at 0x00460D1D** (`BuffManager.cs:670-673`, `CombatManager.cs:1977-1979`) | Defaults **true** (clear) on an engine without the field — caller's interval throttle becomes the only anti-spam guard (`RynthCoreHost.cs:658-663`) |
| **Client hourglass** (`BusyCount`) | event-fed int, NOT polled | AC's `ClientUISystem` busy counter. `>0` = a server action (cast/use/move) is in flight; do **not** send any game action. Fed by `OnBusyCountIncremented/Decremented` events (`CorpseOpenController.cs:98-115`, `PluginExports.cs:79-83`), mirrored onto both managers (`CombatManager.cs:188`, `BuffManager.cs:233`). | Queuing actions onto AC while its action pipeline is mid-flight | `GetBusyState()` (`RynthCoreHost.cs:632-636`) exists but is **never called** by RynthAi — it reads 0 even while AC rejects a cast, so it's the wrong gate. The event-fed count is authoritative. |
| **Server action-done seq** (`UseDoneSeq`) | `GetUseDoneSeq()` — `RynthCoreHost.cs:665-680` (v63+) | Monotonic count of inbound server `UseDone` (GameEvent `0x1C7`). Server bumps it when it **finishes** an action — *completed OR refused*. Snapshot at cast, watch for change = cast resolved on the server. | Pacing offensive casts on **real completion** instead of a blind timer; a turn/stop landing during a server's deferred windup orphans the prior cast → 0 damage (`CombatManager.cs:2668-2673`, `1880-1890`) | Returns 0 when absent → the 2500 ms timeout becomes the sole resolution gate (`CombatManager.cs:2678-2688`) |

> **Contract 0.1 — degrade-open, never spin.** Every gate has a defined "engine lacks this API" behavior (cast-gate → true, UseDone → timeout-only). A port MUST preserve "capability absent ⇒ fall back to the interval/timeout," never "capability absent ⇒ block forever." The 344 `Has*` guard sites exist for exactly this.

> **Contract 0.2 — the two async signals are complementary, not redundant.** `CanCastNow` is a *local client animation* state (available every frame, no network). `UseDoneSeq` is a *server round-trip* completion. The magic path gates the **next** cast on `CanCastNow` (gesture done locally) but gates **motion emission** (turn stops, stance flips, target drops) on `UseDoneSeq`/timeout (server done). In the browser: `CanCastNow` ≈ a locally-computed animation flag; `UseDoneSeq` ≈ counting inbound `0x1C7` messages off the wsbridge drain.

## 1. Target selection & priority

`ScanNearbyTargets` (`CombatManager.cs:516`) pre-filters into `_scannedTargets`; `HandleCombatTrigger` (`:2170`) scores + picks; `Think` (`:1649`) validates the locked target each tick. Selection is **selection-free** (never writes AC's global selection `0x00871E54`) — see §6.

| # | Contract | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | **Scan is debounced, not rate-limited.** Skip re-scan if <50 ms since last (`SCAN_INTERVAL_MS`). It runs at frame rate; 50 ms is a min-interval, not a cadence. | `:518-520`, `:339` |
| T2 | **Filter order (each `continue` is a distinct exclusion class, order matters):** self → not `Monster` class → spell-projectile-name → user "never attack" list → blacklisted → recently-killed → `!ObjectIsAttackable` → `HealthRatio==0` (dead-not-corpse) → distance gate → LOS/raycast. | `:574-641` |
| T3 | **Engaged-target distance hysteresis.** New targets acquired only within `MonsterRange`; the *currently engaged* target is retained out to `DisengageDistance` (`= MonsterDisengageRange` if `>MonsterRange`, else `MonsterRange+3`). Absorbs AC's combat-mode step-back so an edge mob doesn't oscillate engage↔peace. | `:615-622`, `:403-406` |
| T4 | **`ObjectIsAttackable` weenie-null returns *true* (attackable), not false.** The post-login/fresh-spawn window where the client hasn't populated the weenie table must default attackable, or the bot "stares at a monster for 3 s." A stale-ID attack failure is caught downstream by the scan-grace window (T9). | Review §1.2-1.3; `:610` |
| T5 | **Spell projectiles are never targets.** Own bolts/streaks misclassify as `Monster` with no health record — excluded by name test both at scan (`:582`) and at target-validation (`:1729`). | `:582`, `:1729` |
| T6 | **Sort = closest-first, tiebreak by facing angle within 0.5 yd.** Purely for deterministic ordering; the actual pick is score-based. | `:657-662` |
| T7 | **Utility-AI score** = `distScore(0-100) + hpScore(0-50) + threatScore(30 if <3yd else 0) + facingScore(0-10) + priorityScore`. `distScore` linear in remaining range; `hpScore` rewards *lower* HP (finish wounded mobs); `threatScore` flat bonus in melee range; `facingScore` prefers mobs already in front. | `ScoreCandidate` `:2212-2233` |
| T8 | **Monster-rule priority is opt-in above default.** `priorityScore = max(0, rule.Priority-1) * 5`, and only when a *named* (non-`"Default"`) rule substring-matches. `Priority=1` (default) adds 0 — normal grind uses natural "fastest-to-attack" scoring; `Priority=10`→+45; `Priority=20`→+95. (This exact formula was tuned after `Priority*5` over-biased every configured mob — Review §4.4.) | `:2221-2231` |
| T9 | **Target lock + stickiness.** Once picked, `_lockedTargetId` holds; an alternative must beat `locked_score + TARGET_SWITCH_STICKINESS(25)` to steal the lock. Prevents flapping on near-ties. Switch only fires if `bestId != _lockedTargetId`. | `:2182-2189`, `:344` |
| T10 | **Scan-grace window.** A locked target that drops out of `_scannedTargets` (transient LOS/scan gap) is retained for `TARGET_SCAN_GRACE_MS(1500)` before `DropTarget("scan grace expired")` — one bad LOS result must not hand control to navigation mid-fight. | `:1766-1783`, `:159` |
| T11 | **Lock-restore before re-selection.** If `activeTargetId==0` but `_lockedTargetId!=0` (transient world-filter null), restore active from lock *before* `HandleCombatTrigger` so the same tick doesn't pick a different mob. | `:1719-1720` |
| T12 | **Five target-drop conditions, one cleanup.** `DropTarget(reason)` is the single teardown for: blacklisted, became-corpse (class≠Monster), hp=0, out-of-range (>disengage), scan-grace-expired, no-progress-timeout. It zeroes active+locked, facing, fight-tracking, predict-kill arms, stance-recovery episode, and (only if no cast is in flight) clears turn motions. Reason is logged. | `DropTarget` `:1236-1269`; validation `:1722-1740` |
| T13 | **Recently-killed suppression (two TTLs coexist).** A killed id is suppressed from re-acquisition by expiry-time map: confirmed kill = `RECENTLY_KILLED_SUPPRESS_MS(4000)`, predicted-kill swap = `PREDICTED_SWAP_SUPPRESS_MS(2000)`. Needed because the death signal (`KillerNotification 0x01AD`) arrives at the lethal hit, *before* the mob reads HP=0 or reclassifies to a corpse (ACE delays `CreateCorpse` by the full death animation). | `:224-235`, prune at `:539-551` |
| T14 | **No-progress blacklist (time-based, opt-in).** If engaged `> TargetNoProgressTimeoutSec` (default **0 = disabled**) with no damage dealt (ref = last-damage-time, else lock-time), blacklist + drop. Skipped while raycast warming up. | `:1804-1823` |
| T15 | **Blacklist is confirmed-miss-driven, not wall-clock.** `AttemptThreshold=1` (one report → blacklist); the N-cast tolerance lives in the cast-judgement path (`JudgePendingCast`), which only counts a "miss" after `BlacklistCastSettleMs` with no damage. Self-expires on read (`TimeoutSeconds = BlacklistTimeoutSec`, default 30 s). The old dual-blacklist dict was dead code and removed. | `:1663-1664`, `:1725`, Review §2.2b |
| T16 | **`HasNearbyMonsters` ⊃ `HasTargets`.** Nav-blocking counts LOS-blocked mobs (`_nearbyNoLos`) so the bot stops *before* walking into a room; target acquisition does not. | `:358-359`, `:637-641`; Review §2.1 |

## 2. Attack pacing (the gates in action)

### 2a. Magic offensive casts — the deferred-windup discipline
The ACE server defers a **targeted** cast's windup behind a turn-to-face; any turn/stop `MoveToState` that lands during that windup **orphans** the cast (gesture animates, 0 damage, "too busy" forever). Self-buffs are immune (untargeted → synchronous). The entire magic pacing sequence exists to make combat casts behave like the working self-buff path.

| # | Contract | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | **Per-mode attack interval.** Magic uses `AttackSpellIntervalMs` (default **1500**, ≤0 → 1500); melee/missile use **1000 ms**. Offensive casts are spaced ~1-2 s so back-to-back "too busy" refusals don't silently drop casts. | `:1855-1864` |
| P2 | **Cast-cadence guard (magic only).** While a prior cast is still resolving (`IsAwaitingCastResolution`), do **not** turn or issue another cast. Resolves on `UseDoneSeq` change or `CAST_RESOLUTION_TIMEOUT_MS(2500)`. | `:1880-1890`, `IsAwaitingCastResolution` `:2675-2688` |
| P3 | **Settle-before-cast facing (magic only).** If `facingError > FACE_TOLERANCE_DEG(15°)`: keep turning (do NOT "fire anyway" while turning — that was the bug), bounded by `FACE_MAX_WAIT_MS(2500)`. Once within angle: release turn motions, then wait `FACE_SETTLE_MS(140 ms)` (≥ one 30 Hz server tick) for the turn-stop to reach the server **before** the cast packet. | `:1892-1938`, `:129/:140/:141` |
| P4 | **Cast-gesture gate (magic only).** Even after cadence+facing pass, gate the cast on `CastGateWatchdog.CanCastNow` — the `CMotionInterp` gate. Melee/missile are deliberately NOT gated on this (a swing isn't a cast; AC paces the swing animation itself). | `:1973-1991` |
| P5 | **Mark on issue.** Every issued targeted cast calls `MarkCombatCastIssued()`: arms `_awaitingCastResolution`, sets deadline `now+2500 ms`, snapshots `UseDoneSeq`. This is what makes P2/P6 work. | `:2699-2704`, call sites `:2966`,`:3002` |
| P6 | **Motion emitters defer while a cast is in flight.** Peace-mode swap (`:1757`), stance/weapon re-assert (`:1840-1844`), target-switch turn-stop (`:2200`), and `DropTarget`'s turn-stop (`:1268`) all check `IsCastInFlight()` and defer — else they truncate the in-flight gesture and strand server `Player.IsBusy` (relog-only wedge). | `:1757`,`:1840`,`:2200`,`:1268` |
| P7 | **BusyCount hard-stop precedes everything.** `if (BusyCount>0) return` before any attack/cast in the interval branch. | `:1873-1878` |
| P8 | **Equip-gate before cast.** `AttackWithMagic` refuses to cast if a wand equip was issued `<3000 ms` ago (wand may not read as wielded yet). | `:2911-2918` |

### 2b. Physical (melee/missile)
| # | Contract | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P9 | **Melee clears turn motions every tick.** AC auto-orients during the swing; any leftover nav turn spins the character. Melee has **no** explicit face-first. | `:1849-1853` |
| P10 | **Missile facing** uses the lighter `FACE_TIMEOUT_MS(1000)` "fire anyway" gate (not the magic settle gate) — AC paces the missile itself, so windup-orphaning doesn't apply. Requires `HasWieldedAmmo` (ammo detected via `AmmunitionSlot` bit `0x00800000`, name fallback). | `:1943-1963`, `:2740-2801` |
| P11 | **Native vs direct attack (the unsolved facing trade-off).** `UseNativeAttack` default **true**: native pipeline turns-to-face but requires `SelectItem(targetId)` first (the last selection clobber). The direct explicit-target path (`MeleeAttack`/`MissileAttack`, opcodes `0x08`/`0x0A`) is selection-free but does **NOT** turn the character — a port choosing direct MUST build reliable turn-to-face first. | ExplicitTarget doc §3-§6; `AttackTarget` `:2803+` |

### 2c. Kill-shot prediction (selection-free, damage-learned)
| # | Contract | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P12 | **Predict a kill from learned damage.** Combat can't read an unselected mob's live HP (ACE streams vitals only for the selected target). Instead accumulate confirmed per-hit damage (`AttackerNotification 0x01B1`) vs appraised/learned MaxHP; if `remainingHP ≤ avgCastDamage × KILL_CONFIDENCE(0.80)` and `≥ KILL_MIN_SAMPLES(3)` learned hits, arm a swap to the next target. | `:237-307` |
| P13 | **Never drop mid-windup.** The armed swap executes only after the cast windup is **seen animating and then released** (`CanCastNow` false→true), or `PredictKillSwapMaxWaitMs(3000)`. Confirmation that the cast wasn't refused = `OffensiveRefusalWindowMs(500 ms)` elapsed with no "too busy". Dropping at 500 ms aborted high-tier casts mid-windup (2 mobs ping-ponged, nothing died — 2026-06-13). | `:1684-1712`, `:298-305` |

## 3. Buff scheduling

`BuffManager.OnHeartbeat` (`:474`) is the pump. `NeedsAnyBuff` (`:802`) is the arbiter query; `CheckAndCastSelfBuffs` (`:833`) is the caster; `IsBuffActive` (`:1148`) is the per-spell decision; `RefreshFromLiveMemory` (`:1318`) reads `ReadPlayerEnchantments`.

| # | Contract | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | **Login stabilization gate — never buff on a half-streamed registry.** After login the server streams the enchantment registry over seconds. Block ALL casts (`return`) until `RefreshFromLiveMemory` returns the **same count on two consecutive 1 s reads** (registry done streaming), or `LoginRefreshMaxWaitMs(20000)`. Opening early wipes timers → full rebuff every login. `RefreshFromLiveMemory` must NOT set the ready flag itself — only the OnHeartbeat gate owns it. | `:465-519`, `:1394-1397` |
| B2 | **Expiry source of truth: player enchantment registry.** `ReadPlayerEnchantments(spellIds, expiryTimes, max)` + `GetServerTime()`; `remainingSeconds = expiry − serverNow`; drop entries `≤0`. Keyed by **spell family** (`_ramBuffTimers`), not spell id. Requires both `HasReadPlayerEnchantments` and `HasGetServerTime` or returns −1 (no-op). | `RefreshFromLiveMemory` `:1318-1360`, `MaxEnchantments=512` `:1327` |
| B3 | **Rebuff threshold.** `IsBuffActive` returns active while `now < Expiration − RebuffSecondsRemaining` (default **300 s**). Below that window → recast. ⚠ **Discrepancy to preserve deliberately or fix:** the comment at `:1160-1162` claims batch-rebuff overrides this to 1200 s, but `CheckAndCastSelfBuffs`/`AnyBuffBelowThreshold` actually pass `_settings.RebuffSecondsRemaining` uniformly (`:805`,`:828`,`:838`) — the 1200 s override is **not implemented in current code**. A port should use one uniform threshold and treat the comment as stale. | `:1160-1163`,`:805`,`:838` |
| B4 | **Tier-upgrade rule.** If a better-tier spell is now castable than what's active, treat as inactive and recast **regardless of time left** — for both player and item buffs. | `:1165-1180`,`:1211-1215` |
| B5 | **Incantation tier-cap (flap guard).** Many high-tier buffs are Incantations (nominal tier 8) that land skill-capped lower (e.g. "Incantation of Sprint Self" → "Sprint Self VI"). Comparing landed-6 vs nominal-8 recasts forever. Cap the target at the **highest tier actually observed landing** for that family (`_familyAchievedTier`, learned in `RefreshFromLiveMemory`). | `:1200-1215`,`RecordAchievedTier` `:1383` |
| B6 | **Permanent enchant = presence-only.** `remainingSeconds > 86400×365` → record with a sentinel expiration, flagged `IsPermanent`, **not** persisted to disk. Without this the family never records → `IsBuffActive` false → recast every refresh forever. On death/dispel it leaves the registry, the next read drops it, and the bot rebuffs. | `:1362-1386` |
| B7 | **Item/armor enchants tracked separately, chat-confirmed.** Impen/Banes live on the item, are absent from `ReadPlayerEnchantments`, so tracked in `_itemSpellTimers` (keyed by family). Recorded **only on chat confirmation** ("you cast X"), never optimistically — an optimistic timer left a phantom 1 h "active" buff whenever a cast silently failed. Preserved across `RefreshFromLiveMemory` via the `preservedItemTimers` copy. Their true duration is not client-readable (server-authoritative; VTank couldn't either — Review headline). | `:1172-1194`,`:920-925`,`:1335-1343`,`IsItemEnchantment` `:948` |
| B8 | **Cast confirmation splits by kind.** Self-buffs confirm by **re-reading the live registry** after `SelfBuffConfirmMs(600 ms)`; give up at `SelfBuffGiveUpMs(2500 ms)`. Item enchants confirm by **chat** + a no-chat timeout `NoChatResolveTimeoutMs(5000 ms)`. | `:534-566`,`:46`,`:53-54` |
| B9 | **Silent-no-show valve.** After `SilentNoShowThreshold(2)` consecutive self-buff no-shows for a family, park it in `_buffFailCooldownUntil` for `SilentNoShowCooldown(30 min)`; a cold snapshot also marks the id unresolvable (drop a tier). Bounds the "family in the dynamic list that can never land" infinite loop. | `:575-587`,`:157-158` |
| B10 | **Hard-reject cooldown.** A server hard-rejection (no components, etc.) parks the family `BuffFailCooldownSec(120 s)`; auto-batch must **respect** parked families (do not clear cooldowns) or `/god` loops: batch→clear→cast→no-show→re-park. Only explicit `ForceFullRebuff` resets them. | `:883-894`,`:838-853`,`:141` |
| B11 | **Auto batch-rebuff.** When any buff drops below threshold, flip `_isForceRebuffing` to recast **all** buffs in one pass (align timers) — but do NOT clear `_ramBuffTimers` (that's `ForceFullRebuff`'s job; clearing here re-triggers instantly for any unresolvable spell). | `:833-853` |
| B12 | **Force rebuff ignores timers.** While `_isForceRebuffing`, `IsBuffActive` consults only `_forceRebuffCastFamilies` (spells cast *this cycle*), not live timers — the point is to recast everything to a common start. Self-buff confirmation must add the family here or the batch respins it forever. | `:1153-1157`,`:559-564` |
| B13 | **Death/dispel recovery = 30 s periodic re-sync.** No explicit vitae/death event is modeled. Every `PeriodicRefreshIntervalMs(30000)` re-read from live memory; if enchantments left the registry (death), stale in-memory timers are cleared → `NeedsAnyBuff` true → rebuff. This is the *only* mechanism catching "died, lost all buffs, timers still say active." | `:521-531`,`:463` |
| B14 | **Buff pacing reuses the same three gates.** `OnHeartbeat` blocks on `SpellCastIntervalMs` (default **400**, faster than combat's 1500), then `CastGateWatchdog.CanCastNow || BusyCount>0`, pinning `BotAction="Buffing"` so combat can't sneak a peace-mode switch mid-cast. | `:661-684`,`:709-714` |

### Vital/heal thresholds (`CheckVitals` `:717`)
| # | Contract | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| B15 | **Emergency HP override.** `HP ≤ 30% && stam > 20%` → cast "Stamina to Health Self" regardless of mode/config — sits below the configurable thresholds so a "do nothing" config still survives. | `:730-737` |
| B16 | **In-combat vs idle threshold sets.** `inCombat = HasCloseThreat(MonsterRange)`. In-combat reacts at LOW thresholds (`HealAt=60`, `GetManaAt=40`, `RestamAt=30`); idle tops up to HIGH (`TopOffHP/Stam/Mana=95`). Strict `<`; set 0 to disable a vital. Mana-recharge (Stam→Mana) additionally requires `stam > 15`. Health kits tried before Heal Self. | `:739-762`,`:759`, settings `LegacyUiSettings.cs:95-100` |

## 4. Stance / combat-mode transitions

`CurrentCombatMode` is read **live** from AC every access (no cached field — event-drop drift eliminated, Review §2.2e). Mode ∈ {NonCombat, Melee, Missile, Magic}.

| # | Contract | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | **Live mode read.** `CurrentCombatMode => HasGetCurrentCombatMode ? GetCurrentCombatMode() : NonCombat`. Never trust a cached mode across a tick. | `:182-184` |
| S2 | **AC invariant: weapon-wielded ↔ mode-matches.** `EquipWeaponAndSetStance` desired mode derives from the weapon: wand→Magic, MissileWeapon→Missile, else Melee. If already in the desired mode with the wand wielded, it's a no-op (never `UseObject` an already-wielded wand — AC treats that as an unwield/MOVE). | `:2307-2327`,`:2386-2395` |
| S3 | **Bow→wand needs dequip-first.** Stock ACE refuses to auto-dequip a main-hand bow for a Held-slot wand (`CheckWeaponCollision`) AND denies `ChangeCombatMode(Magic)` while the bow is wielded. Sequence: `CancelAttack`+`StopCompletely` → stow bow into an open pack → `UseObject(wand)` → only request Magic once the wand reads wielded (next tick). `CombatBowDequipMaxAttempts(3)`, `WandSwapWieldResolveMs(4000)`. | `:2397-2429`,`:81-93` |
| S4 | **Missile mode requires ammo.** Never enter Missile mode without `HasWieldedAmmo()` — AC rejects it and cycles stance. | `:2318-2321`,`:1961-1963` |
| S5 | **Stance-flip exponential backoff.** `StanceRetryDelayMs = min(15000, 1000×2^min(4, attempts/4))` — doubles every 4 failed sends, capped 15 s; one-shot warning at 16 consecutive sends. Prevents the 2026-05-25 "256 consecutive ChangeCombatMode → client death" crash class. | `:44-55` |
| S6 | **Cross-subsystem weapon-swap serializer.** Buff and combat share one `WeaponSwapGate`; a swap is denied unless `≥ MinIntervalMs(3000)` since the last swap by anyone. AC allows only one item action in flight; two `UseObject` equips within ~1 s trigger "you can only move or use one item at a time" and a worst-case `DBOCache::DestroyObj` AV. Casts and non-weapon item actions do NOT go through it. | `WeaponSwapGate.cs:22-52`,`:33` |
| S7 | **Idle → peace.** No valid target + `PeaceModeWhenIdle`(default true) + empty scan + `BusyCount==0` → `ChangeCombatMode(NonCombat)`, throttled 500 ms, deferred while a cast is in flight. Stops the client auto-running toward a distant mob. | `:1746-1762` |

## 5. Error recovery / watchdogs

| # | Contract | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | **Cast-gate stuck backstop (`CastGateWatchdog`).** `CanCastNow` reads `[CMI+0x80]`; a server-refused "too busy" can leave a one-shot motion node that never pops, freezing the bot standing still (no watchdog in the engine). If the raw gate stays closed continuously `> StuckMs(4000)`, declare it stuck and report clear; keep reporting clear until the raw gate genuinely recovers (`raw==true`). Safe because `SpellCastIntervalMs` throttle + "too busy" PARK remain the anti-spam guarantees. Static/shared across buff+combat. | `CastGateWatchdog.cs:24-67` |
| E2 | **Stance-deadlock recovery (bounded re-equip).** When the wand reads wielded but AC refuses the mode flip: after `StanceStuckRecoverMs(8000)` stuck, `ForceResetBusyCount()` + `UseObject(wand)` to resync — but capped at `StanceReEquipMaxAttempts(2)`. UseObject on an already-wielded wand is a MOVE; spamming it jammed AC's item queue permanently (17 min → relog-only, 2026-06-11). Past the cap: mode-change-only + one-shot user warning. This is the **only** `ForceResetBusyCount` call in the combat hot path. | `:2335-2369`,`:2354`,`:62-78`; `BuffStanceStuckRecoverMs(8000)`/`BuffStanceReEquipMax(2)` mirror it `BuffManager.cs:1927-1928` |
| E3 | **`ForceResetBusyCount` semantics.** Fire-and-forget host call (`RynthCoreHost.cs:638-642`) that zeroes AC's engine busy count. Callers ALSO manually zero both managers' `BusyCount` fields alongside it (the event-fed mirror won't correct on its own). Exposed to the user as `/ra clearbusy` — the documented manual escape hatch for a stuck busy count. | `RynthAiCommands.cs:1626-1658` |
| E4 | **Cadence self-clears — no permanent in-flight.** `IsAwaitingCastResolution` clears on `UseDoneSeq` advance OR the 2500 ms deadline; a missing/forever server-done can't wedge the cast serializer. | `:2675-2688` |
| E5 | **Predicted-swap arm self-expires.** If the target advanced/dropped or the arm is stale, `_predictKillSwapArmed=false`; timeout `PredictKillSwapMaxWaitMs(3000)` guarantees a missing gesture can't arm-lock combat. Wrong predictions expire unrecorded. | `:1692-1711`,`:256-303` |
| E6 | **Raycast-ready clean slate.** On the raycast warmup→ready edge, clear blacklist + miss/no-progress timers once — mobs sidelined while targeting was degraded get re-evaluated instead of stuck for 5 min. | `:527-537` |
| E7 | **Macro-off transition.** On running→stopped, clear turn motions **once** (not every frame — that blocks manual keyboard turning); combat/buff `OnHeartbeat` early-return while stopped. | `:2104-2115`,`BuffManager.cs:486` |
| E8 | **Every phase is try/caught in the pump.** `ScanNearbyTargets`, `Think` each wrapped so one crash doesn't kill the tick; skip-reasons recorded to `LastCombatSkipReason`/`LastBuffSkipReason` for `/ra why`. | `:1715`,`:2126-2166`, skip-reason sites throughout |

## 6. Selection-free invariant (cross-cutting)

> **Contract X1.** Combat targeting must **never** write AC's single global selection (`0x00871E54`). All per-tick `SelectItem` calls were removed 2026-06-03; casts use explicit-target `FreeHandsAndCastSpell(spellId, targetId)`, physical attacks pass `targetId` as an arg. The lone remaining clobber is the **native** physical-attack path (`SelectItem` before `NativeAttack`, `CombatManager.cs:~1609`), retained only because that AC pipeline has no target argument and needs selection to face+swing. Self-buffs cast with `targetId=0`. A browser port has no shared-selection constraint, so it should implement the explicit-target shape directly and skip native entirely. (ExplicitTarget doc §2-§4, §6.)

## 8. Portability notes for the browser target

- **Poll→async is manageable here** because the whole design is *already* a set of self-clearing timers + capability guards, not a blocking state machine. Each contract is "check gate(s), act or return this tick." A rAF/message-drain loop calling `Think()`/`OnHeartbeat()` reproduces it; the host's `TryGet*`/fire-and-forget shape maps onto poll-only `SessionHandle` methods + JS globals.
- **The three gates map to web signals:** `CanCastNow` ≈ a locally-derived animation/casting flag on `SessionHandle`; `BusyCount` ≈ counting AC busy inc/dec events off the session; `UseDoneSeq` ≈ counting inbound `UseDone (0x1C7)` protocol messages drained through `holtburger-wsbridge`. All three degrade-open (Contract 0.1) — a web port that hasn't wired one yet should hard-code the "absent" fallback, not block.
- **Drop native attack + the selection clobber entirely** (Contract X1 / P11): the web client has no shared inventory-selection constraint, so implement the explicit-target cast/attack shape and the settle-before-cast facing (P3) from day one.
- **Item-enchant durations are unknowable client-side** (B7) — carry the cast-time-record approach; don't spend effort trying to read armor-cast timers.
